$description: Roles. Each holds its light value in $value and its dark value in $extensions["io.github.neatlittlemacapps.nigari.dark"]: one token, two themes (FR-002). A colour role names a palette step ("{palette.raspberry.500}") per theme, with io.github.neatlittlemacapps.nigari.alpha where it is translucent; never a hex (spec 019). To give a role another colour, point its tokens at another palette (primary, primary-hover, primary-pressed, primary-subtle together), or change that palette's base in primitives.tokens.json; the build checks contrast on the result. io.github.neatlittlemacapps.nigari.css keeps the name styles.css already reads.

primary.$description: The one accent: links, the chosen item, the main action. Text-safe on every surface in both themes.

primary-hover.$description: Primary under the pointer: one step further from the surface. Also the text of a primary outline or low button under the pointer, on its own wash: checked there (spec 020).

primary-pressed.$description: Primary while pressed or switched on: two steps further from the surface.

primary-subtle.$description: A wash of primary behind a chosen row or chip.

on-primary.$description: Text and icons on a primary fill.

destructive.$description: Deleting and other actions that cannot be undone. Text-safe on every surface in both themes.

destructive-hover.$description: Destructive under the pointer. Also the text of a destructive outline or low button under the pointer, on its own wash: checked there (spec 020).

destructive-subtle.$description: A wash of destructive behind a warning.

on-destructive.$description: Text and icons on a destructive fill.

rank.$description: A workspace role's level as a fill (Manage users, the role ToggleGroup): the further a role reaches, the warmer the colour. Not decoration: in a row of four equal choices the chosen level would otherwise show only as a fill, and which level reaches further would not show at all. No access is grey, never the accent: a coloured chip reading "no access" says the opposite of what it means (owner, spec 020: keep the rank colours).

on-rank.$description: Text on a rank fill: white in both themes, checked against every rank.

sidebar.$description: The sidebar: one step off the document.

glass.$description: Nearly opaque on purpose: at 82% a menu over a code block showed a smudge of it through the blur.

muted.$description: Solid, never alpha: an emoji is drawn in the text colour's alpha. Steps 525/475 rather than the bases: at 500 the sidebar's labels and its Search box read 4.1 to 4.4:1 in light and a board card's labels 4.2:1 in dark (#527, #761).

default.$description: Today's name, kept for the stylesheets that read it: an alias of color.primary (spec 019).

soft.$description: Today's name, kept for the stylesheets that read it: an alias of color.primary-subtle (spec 019).

danger.$description: Today's name, kept for the stylesheets that read it: an alias of color.destructive (spec 019).

focus.$description: The focus ring. The accent today; a token of its own so it can change without the accent.

hover.$description: Pointing: a faint wash over whatever is underneath.

default.$description: Hairlines, not borders: alpha, so one value reads right on paper, sidebar and card.
The primary action is ink, as on the site: a filled pill in the text colour.

text.$description: Text on the ink pill: the paper in light, near-black in dark.

data.$description: Data roles: what charts draw with (spec 019, R5). Each names a data palette's step per theme; every drawn colour reaches 3:1 on the document and on cards in both themes (spec 004). The colours a select option stores (selectOptions.ts) are data, not tokens: chartTheme.ts maps each to a data role.

strong.$description: The strongest shade: the largest group of a sorted chart.

soft.$description: The softest shade that still passes 3:1; the same colour as the hue's chart series, so an option keeps its colour across palettes.
